1	\section{Physical spatial pairings and the full occupation class}
     2	\label{S:spatial-occupation-foundation}
     3	
     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict
     8	inequality used in the scalar powers and concavity. The finite variational value
     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of
    10	Proposition~\ref{P:variational-positive-scores}.
    11	
    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}
    34	
    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.
    39	
    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
    99	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   100	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   101	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   102	  a positive finite real number, and
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   104	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   105	    k\left[
   106	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   107	    \right]^{1/k}.
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	\end{proposition}
   110	
   111	\begin{proof}
   112	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   113	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   114	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   115	  autocorrelation argument in the preceding proof gives $0 < A: =
   116	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) < \infty$. With $U_\ell g(x) = \ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the
   117	  physical changes of variables give
   118	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   119	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   120	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   121	  \end{equation}
   122	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   123	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   124	
   125	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   126	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   127	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   128	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   129	  \[
   130	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   131	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   132	  \]
   133	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   134	  gives
   135	  \[
   136	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   137	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   138	  \]
   139	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   140	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   141	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. The already finite
   142	  $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ bounds every ratio by
   143	  $8M_aq^{q/2}(S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}/k)^k/\alpha^{\alpha/2}$. A normalized compact
   144	  bump supplies a positive ratio. This proves positivity and finiteness of $R_0$
   145	  before any rough spatial extension is invoked. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   147	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]
   150	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   151	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   152	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   153	  \begin{align}
   154	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   155	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   156	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   157	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   158	  \end{align}
   159	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   160	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   161	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   162	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   163	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   164	  \end{equation}
   165	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   166	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   167	\end{proposition}
   168	
   169	\begin{proof}
   170	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   171	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   172	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   173	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   174	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   175	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   176	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   177	  convention gives
   178	  \[
   179	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   180	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   181	  \]
   182	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   183	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   184	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   185	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   186	  \[
   187	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   188	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   189	  \]
   190	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   191	
   192	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   193	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   194	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   195	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   196	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   197	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   198	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   199	
   200	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   201	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   202	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   203	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   204	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   205	  continuity.
   206	
   207	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   208	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   209	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   210	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   211	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   212	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   213	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   214	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   215	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   216	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   217	
   218	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   219	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   220	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   221	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   222	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   223	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   224	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   225	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   226	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   227	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   228	\end{proof}

   230	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   231	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   232	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   233	  \[
   234	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   235	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   236	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   237	  \]
   238	  Then
   239	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   240	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   241	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   242	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   243	    \in(0,\infty).
   244	  \end{equation}
   245	  In particular,
   246	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   247	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   248	    \qquad
   249	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   250	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   251	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   252	  \end{equation}
   253	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   254	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   255	\end{proposition}
   256	
   257	\begin{proof}
   258	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   259	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   260	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   261	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   262	  \[
   263	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   264	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   265	  \]
   266	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   267	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   268	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   269	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   270	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   271	  \[
   272	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   273	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   274	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   275	  \]
   276	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   277	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   278	\end{proof}

   280	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   281	
   282	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   283	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   284	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   285	  \int_0^\infty
   286	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   287	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   288	\end{equation}
   289	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   290	
   291	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   292	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   293	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   294	  $[0,1]$ is
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   296	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   297	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   298	  \end{equation}
   299	\end{lemma}
   300	
   301	\begin{proof}
   302	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   303	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   304	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   305	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   306	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   307	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   308	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   309	\end{proof}
   310	
   311	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   312	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   313	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   314	optimizer condition is imposed.
   315	
   316	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   317	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   318	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   319	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   320	  \[
   321	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   322	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   323	  \]
   324	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   325	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   326	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   327	  \end{equation}
   328	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   329	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   330	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   331	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   332	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   333	  \end{equation}
   334	\end{proposition}
   335	
   336	\begin{proof}
   337	  The map $s\mapsto b(g_s)$ is measurable by continuity of the squared gradient
   338	  norm. Also $\int_0^1\|g_s\|_{H^1}^2\ud s = 1+T(g)$. Use a separably valued
   339	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   340	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   341	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   342	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   343	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   344	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.
   345	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} makes every pairing independent of the
   346	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   347	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   348	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical
   349	  integral.
   350	
   351	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}
   352	  and~\eqref{E:spatial-square-CS} give $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   353	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}F(s)F(t)$. Since $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$, concavity on the unit time
   354	  interval yields $\int_0^1F^2 = \int_0^1b(g_s)^{\alpha/2}\ud s \le
   355	  T(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Now use $2F(s)F(t) \le F(s)^2+F(t)^2$ and the exact row
   356	  bound \eqref{E:occupation-kernel-row}, whose column bound is the same because
   357	  $K_\star$ is even, to obtain \eqref{E:occupation-physical-bound}. Positive
   358	  Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known. Null-time modifications affect
   359	  only a product-null set, so they cannot change $J$.
   360	
   361	  The scalar maximum of $R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T^{\alpha/2}-T/2$ over $T \ge 0$
   362	  is $R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$, by the same
   363	  differentiation as~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This bounds the occupation
   364	  supremum from above. For positivity take a constant-in-time unit compact
   365	  profile and its spatial dilation $U_\ell$. Its $J$ is $J_0\ell^\alpha
   366	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$, where $J_0 = \int_0^1\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud s\ud t \in
   367	  (0,\infty)$, while $T = \ell^2b(g)$. For sufficiently small $\ell > 0$,
   368	  $\alpha < 2$ makes $J-T/2 > 0$. Thus, the nonempty supremum is a positive
   369	  finite real number. This is a comparison bound; no attaining profile or
   370	  equality in it has been asserted. No spatial point trace or rough stochastic
   371	  evolution was used. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}.
   372	\end{proof}
   373	
   374	For zero covariance all spatial pairings vanish and set $R_{\mathrm{sp}} = 0$.
   375	The spatial and occupation energies are zero suprema of $-b/2$ and $-T/2$: small
   376	spatial dilations of one fixed unit compact profile make these energies tend to
   377	zero, with the profile constant in time for the latter. No zero-gradient unit
   378	state is used. The temporal identities remain valid, and the moment model is the
   379	free case already treated.

     4	Retain a nonzero original covariance from Hypothesis~\ref{H:homog} with its
     5	amplitude. Set $a = \alpha_0$, $k = 3-\alpha > 1$, $q = 4-\alpha = k+1$ and $D =
     6	q-2a > 0$. The scalar $D$ is fixed. All profiles are real. The original positive
     7	temporal exponent and threshold imply $\alpha < 2$; this is the strict

     9	over nonnegative controls $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ is that of

    12	\begin{lemma}[The physical two-point integral]\label{L:spatial-physical-pair}
    13	  The positive measure $\nu(\ud x,\ud y) = \ud x\,\Gamma(\ud y)$ is
    14	  sigma-finite. For nonnegative functions define
    15	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-physical-pair}
    16	    B_\Gamma(f,h)=\int f(x)h(x-y)\nu(\ud x,\ud y)
    17	  \end{equation}
    18	  initially as an extended nonnegative integral, using finite Borel
    19	  representatives of Lebesgue classes. Its value is representative independent.
    20	  Lebesgue-a.e. convergence transfers to $\nu$-a.e. convergence at both
    21	  positions $x$ and $x-y$.
    22	\end{lemma}
    23	
    24	\begin{proof}
    25	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ gives sigma-finiteness on exhausting balls, and
    26	  Lebesgue measure is sigma-finite. If $N$ is Borel and Lebesgue null, Tonelli
    27	  applied first in $x$ gives $\nu\{x\in N\} = 0$ and $\nu\{x-y\in N\} = 0$,
    28	  because every fixed translate of $N$ is null. An arbitrary Lebesgue null set
    29	  has a Borel null superset. Thus, arbitrary versions are measurable in the
    30	  $\nu$ completion with the same value, and the same observation applies to the
    31	  exceptional sets of a.e. convergence. Signed pairings will be used only after
    32	  absolute convergence. This proves Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}.
    33	\end{proof}

    35	Put $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) = B_\Gamma(g^2,g^2)$ and $b(g) = \|\nabla g\|_2^2$ on
    36	$H^1$; initially $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ is used only for smooth compact profiles
    37	before the extension below. For smooth compact $z$, write $U_z = \Gamma*z$ in
    38	its usual pointwise sense.

    40	\begin{lemma}[Smooth temporal controls]\label{L:spatial-static-controls}
    41	  For every nonnegative nonzero $z \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$, let
    42	  \[
    43	    \lambda_z(c)^2=
    44	    \sup_{\substack{g\in H^1(\R^d;\R)\\\|g\|_2=1}}
    45	    \left(c\int U_zg^2-b(g)\right),\qquad c>0.
    46	  \]
    47	  This is positive and finite, and $\lambda_z$ is Lipschitz on every compact
    48	  positive $c$ interval. With the exact $M_a$
    49	  in~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-mass},
    50	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-score}
    51	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
    52	    \lambda_z(1)-\frac{M_a}{2}B_\Gamma(z,z).
    53	  \end{equation}
    54	\end{lemma}
    55	
    56	\begin{proof}
    57	  Choose nonnegative nonzero $f \in C_c^\infty(0,1)$ and $s_0 = 1/2$. Let
    58	  $k_f(s_0) = \int_0^1|s_0-t|^{-a}f(t)\ud t > 0$. The smooth test $\Psi(t,x) =
    59	  cf(t)z(x)/k_f(s_0)$ has mean $cU_z$ at $s_0$.
    60	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-unmasked-rate} gives boundedness of this
    61	  potential, the displayed real Rayleigh formula, and a positive rate for every
    62	  $c > 0$. Comparing identical unit tests makes $\lambda_z(c)^2$ Lipschitz with
    63	  constant $\|U_z\|_\infty$. On a positive compact interval its rate has a
    64	  positive floor by monotonicity, giving the square-root Lipschitz bound.
    65	
    66	  Use the nonincreasing smooth cutoff $\chi$ constructed in the proof of
    67	  Proposition~\ref{P:variational-remove-mask}. For integers $n \ge 4$, set on
    68	  $(0,1)$
    69	  \[
    70	    f_n(t)=f_a(t)\chi(1/(nt))\chi(1/(n(1-t))),\qquad
    71	    k_n(s)=\int_0^1|s-t|^{-a}f_n(t)\ud t.
    72	  \]
    73	  Extend $f_n$ by zero. It is smooth compact, vanishes near both endpoints, is
    74	  nonzero, and increases to $f_a$. Thus, $\Psi_n = f_n\otimes z$ is a positive
    75	  smooth control. Monotone convergence
    76	  and~\eqref{E:temporal-equilibrium-potential} give $k_n(s)\uparrow1$ for every
    77	  $s \in [0,1]$. Since the kernel is at least one on the unit square off its
    78	  null diagonal, $0 < c_0: = \int_0^1f_4 \le k_n(s) \le 1$. The mean is
    79	  $k_n(s)U_z$; hence its rate is $\lambda_z(k_n(s))$, converging to
    80	  $\lambda_z(1)$ and bounded by that finite number. Dominated convergence gives
    81	  $I_{\Psi_n} \to \lambda_z(1)$.
    82	
    83	  The Gaussian cost is exactly the nonnegative Tonelli pairing
    84	  \[
    85	    v_{\Psi_n}=B_\Gamma(z,z)\int_0^1f_n(s)k_n(s)\ud s.
    86	  \]
    87	  Its time integrand increases to $f_a$, so the cost tends to
    88	  $M_aB_\Gamma(z,z)$. The spatial factor is finite and positive: its smooth
    89	  compact autocorrelation is positive near zero, and homogeneity scales any
    90	  origin-centered ball of positive $\Gamma$ mass to every other positive radius.
    91	  Such a ball exists by exhaustion. Take the limit of the individual
    92	  inequalities $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}} \ge I_{\Psi_n}-v_{\Psi_n}/2$. The variational
    93	  expression differences need not increase. No control depends on original large
    94	  time and no rough stochastic evolution has been used. This proves
    95	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls}.
    96	\end{proof}

    98	\begin{proposition}[The finite smooth spatial ratio]
    99	  \label{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}
   100	  For real unit $g \in C_c^\infty(\R^d)$ put $R(g) =
   101	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)/b(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Its supremum $R_0$ over these profiles is
   102	  a positive finite real number, and
   103	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-smooth-score}
   104	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge
   105	    k\left[
   106	    \frac{R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}}{8M_aq^{q/2}}
   107	    \right]^{1/k}.
   108	  \end{equation}
   109	\end{proposition}
   110	
   111	\begin{proof}
   112	  The gradient energy $b(g)$ is positive: a nonzero $L^2$ function with zero
   113	  weak gradient would have Fourier transform supported only at zero, and hence
   114	  would vanish. Its square is nonnegative nonzero smooth compact, so the
   115	  autocorrelation argument in the preceding proof gives $0 < A: =
   116	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g) < \infty$. With $U_\ell g(x) = \ell^{d/2}g(\ell x)$, the
   117	  physical changes of variables give
   118	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-dilation}
   119	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(U_\ell g)=\ell^\alpha A,\qquad
   120	    b(U_\ell g)=\ell^2b(g).
   121	  \end{equation}
   122	  The factors in the first identity are $\ell^{2d}$ from the two squares,
   123	  $\ell^{-d}$ from $\ud x$, and $\ell^{\alpha-d}$ from the Radon pushforward.
   124	
   125	  For $\theta,\ell > 0$ choose the smooth control $z = \theta(U_\ell g)^2$. The
   126	  Rayleigh test $U_\ell g$ gives $\lambda_z(1)^2 \ge \theta\ell^\alpha
   127	  A-\ell^2b$, while $B_\Gamma(z,z) = \theta^2\ell^\alpha A$. For any $L > 0$,
   128	  put $u = \alpha/q > 0$ and choose
   129	  \[
   130	    \ell^2=uL^2/b,\qquad
   131	    \theta=(1+u)L^2/(\ell^\alpha A).
   132	  \]
   133	  The radicand is $L^2$. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-static-controls} consequently
   134	  gives
   135	  \[
   136	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge L-CL^q,\qquad
   137	    C=\frac{M_a(1+u)^2}{2R(g)u^{\alpha/2}}>0.
   138	  \]
   139	  Its maximum occurs at $L^k = 1/(qC)$ and is $(k/q)(qC)^{-1/k}$. Since $1+u =
   140	  4/q$, $1/(q^qC) = R(g)\alpha^{\alpha/2}/(8M_aq^{q/2})$,
   141	  proving~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score}. The already finite
   142	  $S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}$ bounds every ratio by
   143	  $8M_aq^{q/2}(S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}/k)^k/\alpha^{\alpha/2}$. A normalized compact
   144	  bump supplies a positive ratio. This proves positivity and finiteness of $R_0$
   145	  before any rough spatial extension is invoked. This proves
   146	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-smooth-ratio}.
   147	\end{proof}

   149	\begin{proposition}[The physical four-linear extension]

150	  \label{P:spatial-four-linear}
   151	  For real $f \in H^1(\R^d)$ define $N(f) = \|f\|_2^{1-\alpha/4}\|\nabla
   152	  f\|_2^{\alpha/4}$. Every physical square pairing is finite and
   153	  \begin{align}
   154	    A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)&\le R_0N(f)^4,\label{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}\\
   155	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   156	    &\le\sqrt{A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)A_{\mathrm{sp}}(h)}.
   157	    \label{E:spatial-square-CS}
   158	  \end{align}
   159	  The signed integral $C_4(f_1,f_2,f_3,f_4) = B_\Gamma(f_1f_2,f_3f_4)$ is
   160	  absolutely convergent and jointly continuous on $(H^1)^4$, with
   161	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-four-linear}
   162	    \int|f_1(x)f_2(x)f_3(x-y)f_4(x-y)|\ud\nu
   163	    \le R_0\prod_{j=1}^4N(f_j).
   164	  \end{equation}
   165	  The ratio supremum $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ over all real unit $H^1$ profiles equals
   166	  $R_0$. Every nonzero $H^1$ profile has $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) > 0$.
   167	\end{proposition}
   168	
   169	\begin{proof}
   170	  For smooth compact $f$, normalization in $R_0$ proves
   171	  \eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}, including $f = 0$. All exponents in $N$
   172	  are positive and $N(f) \le \|f\|_{H^1}$. For smooth compact signed $Q,P$, the
   173	  absolute correlation is compactly supported and bounded by $\|Q\|_2\|P\|_2$.
   174	  Local finiteness of $\Gamma$ therefore makes its physical integral finite.
   175	  Smooth signed covariance is positive: with the ordinary transform
   176	  $\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi) = \int e^{i\xi\cdot x}Q(x)\ud x$, the model
   177	  convention gives
   178	  \[
   179	    B_\Gamma(Q,Q)=\int|\widehat{Q}_{\mathrm{ord}}(\xi)|^2\mu(\ud\xi)
   180	    \ge0,\qquad Q\in C_c^\infty(\R^d;\R).
   181	  \]
   182	  Pair $\Gamma$ with the smooth compact correlation to obtain this identity;
   183	  rapid Fourier decay and tempered $\mu$ give finiteness. Evenness of $\Gamma$
   184	  and $(x,y)\mapsto(x-y,-y)$ give symmetry. The quadratic polynomial for $Q+tP$
   185	  gives covariance Cauchy--Schwarz. In particular, for smooth real $f,h$,
   186	  \[
   187	    0\le B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2)
   188	    \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2.
   189	  \]
   190	  The squares of signed smooth profiles are already smooth and nonnegative.
   191	
   192	  Smooth compact functions are dense in $H^1$. Cutoffs equal to one on the
   193	  radius-$R$ ball, vanishing beyond $2R$ and with gradient at most $C/R$,
   194	  converge by the function and gradient tails and the bound $C\|f\|_2/R$ for the
   195	  extra gradient term. Mollification then converges in $H^1$ by $L^2$
   196	  translation continuity of the function and its weak gradients. The space is
   197	  separable through its closed isometric image $f\mapsto(f,\nabla f)$ in
   198	  $L^2(\R^d)^{d+1}$.
   199	
   200	  For arbitrary $f,h \in H^1$ take smooth approximants converging in $H^1$ and
   201	  along a common subsequence Lebesgue-a.e. Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair}
   202	  transfers this convergence at both positions to $\nu$-a.e. convergence. Fatou
   203	  and continuity of $N$ give $B_\Gamma(f^2,h^2) \le R_0N(f)^2N(h)^2 < \infty$,
   204	  including the diagonal bound. At this stage Fatou supplies an inequality, not
   205	  continuity.
   206	
   207	  Apply ordinary Cauchy--Schwarz under the positive measure $\nu$ to
   208	  $f_1(x)f_3(x-y)$ and $f_2(x)f_4(x-y)$. The two squared integrals are finite by
   209	  the last bound; their square root is at most $R_0\prod_jN(f_j)$. This
   210	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-four-linear}, absolute convergence and multilinearity.
   211	  Telescoping a difference one argument at a time and using $N(f) \le
   212	  \|f\|_{H^1}$ proves joint continuity. Thus, $A_{\mathrm{sp}}$ and the square
   213	  pairings are continuous. PSD for smooth compact profiles passes to finite
   214	  linear combinations of $H^1$ squares by this continuity, and its two-profile
   215	  Cauchy--Schwarz gives \eqref{E:spatial-square-CS}. This completes the physical
   216	  pairing argument beyond Fatou.
   217	
   218	  Every real unit $H^1$ profile has positive gradient energy by the Fourier
   219	  argument above. The homogeneous bound gives $R_{\mathrm{sp}} \le R_0$, and
   220	  smooth inclusion gives the reverse. Normalized smooth approximations preserve
   221	  the ratio by continuity. Finally, for nonzero $f$, choose a bounded set $E$ of
   222	  finite positive measure where $|f| \ge c > 0$. The correlation of $1_E$ is
   223	  continuous and positive near zero by $L^2$ translation continuity. An
   224	  origin-centered ball there has positive $\Gamma$ mass, so $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f)
   225	  \ge c^4B_\Gamma(1_E,1_E) > 0$. This uses a nonnegative integral, not an $H^1$
   226	  claim for $1_E$. Finiteness was already proved. This proves
   227	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   228	\end{proof}
   229	
   230	\begin{proposition}[The spatial energy and static lower variational expression]
   231	  \label{P:spatial-energy-map}
   232	  Over all real unit $H^1$ profiles define the energy
   233	  \[
   234	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   235	    =\sup_{\|g\|_2=1}
   236	    \left(A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)-\frac{b(g)}2\right).
   237	  \]
   238	  Then
   239	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-energy-map}
   240	    \mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}
   241	    =\frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   242	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}^{2/(2-\alpha)}
   243	    \in(0,\infty).
   244	  \end{equation}
   245	  In particular,
   246	  \begin{equation}\label{E:spatial-static-energy-score}
   247	    S_1^{\mathrm{pos}}\ge M_a^{-1/k}F_0(\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}),
   248	    \qquad
   249	    F_0(z)=k\left[
   250	    \frac{(2z/(2-\alpha))^{(2-\alpha)/2}}{8q^{q/2}}
   251	    \right]^{1/k},\quad z>0.
   252	  \end{equation}
   253	  The subscript in $F_0$ labels this scalar map; the covariance retains its
   254	  original temporal exponent $a$.
   255	\end{proposition}
   256	
   257	\begin{proof}
   258	  Physical change of variables, or smooth approximation and
   259	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}, extends \eqref{E:spatial-dilation} to
   260	  real $H^1$ profiles. For fixed unit $g$, with $A,b > 0$, the maximum of
   261	  $\ell^\alpha A-\ell^2b/2$ occurs at $\ell^{2-\alpha} = \alpha A/b$ and equals
   262	  \[
   263	    \frac{2-\alpha}{2}\alpha^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}
   264	    R(g)^{2/(2-\alpha)}.
   265	  \]
   266	  Dilation preserves the whole unit class and includes $\ell = 1$. Taking both
   267	  numerical suprema, then profiles with ratio tending to $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$,
   268	  proves~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. No optimizer is assumed. Smooth ratios
   269	  also approach $R_{\mathrm{sp}}$ by Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear}.
   270	  Pass them through~\eqref{E:spatial-smooth-score} and substitute
   271	  \[
   272	    R_{\mathrm{sp}}\alpha^{\alpha/2}
   273	    =\left(\frac{2\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}}{2-\alpha}
   274	    \right)^{(2-\alpha)/2}.
   275	  \]
   276	  This gives~\eqref{E:spatial-static-energy-score}. This proves
   277	  Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-energy-map}.
   278	\end{proof}

280	\subsection{The kernel row and full occupation energy}
   281	
   282	Define, for $u \ne 0$,
   283	\begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-damped-kernel}
   284	  K_\star(u)=\frac1{\Gamma_E(a)}
   285	  \int_0^\infty
   286	  e^{-(\lambda+\lambda^2/(2D))|u|}
   287	  \lambda^{a-1}\ud\lambda,
   288	\end{equation}
   289	and set $K_\star(0) = 0$ for time integration.
   290	
   291	\begin{lemma}[Exact row maximum]\label{L:occupation-kernel-row}
   292	  The kernel is even, positive off zero, locally integrable, decreasing on
   293	  $(0,\infty)$, and $K_\star(u) \le |u|^{-a}$ off zero. Its exact row maximum on
   294	  $[0,1]$ is
   295	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-kernel-row}
   296	    \max_{s\in[0,1]}\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud t
   297	    =R_\star:=2\int_0^{1/2}K_\star(u)\ud u\in(0,\infty).
   298	  \end{equation}
   299	\end{lemma}
   300	
   301	\begin{proof}
   302	  Dropping the positive quadratic damping bounds the mixture by the Gamma
   303	  integral $|u|^{-a}$. Positivity and monotonicity follow directly from the
   304	  integrand, and $a < 1$ gives local integrability. Put $\Phi(t) =
   305	  \int_0^tK_\star(u)\ud u$. It is concave because its integrand is decreasing on
   306	  positive arguments. The row is $\Phi(s)+\Phi(1-s) \le 2\Phi(1/2)$, with
   307	  equality at $s = 1/2$. The diagonal value changes no time integral. This
   308	  proves Lemma~\ref{L:occupation-kernel-row}.
   309	\end{proof}
   310	
   311	Let $\mathcal{O}$ be the full class of strongly $H^1(\R^d;\R)$-measurable fields
   312	$s\mapsto g_s$ on $(0,1)$ with $\|g_s\|_2 = 1$ a.e. and $T(g) =
   313	\int_0^1b(g_s)\ud s < \infty$. No time smoothness, common compact support or
   314	optimizer condition is imposed.
   315	
   316	\begin{proposition}[The full physical occupation class]
   317	  \label{P:occupation-physical-class}
   318	  The pairings $(s,t)\mapsto B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)$ are measurable,
   319	  representative independent and equal to their physical integrals. With
   320	  \[
   321	    J(g)=\int_0^1\int_0^1
   322	    K_\star(s-t)B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2)\ud s\ud t,
   323	  \]
   324	  every $g \in \mathcal{O}$ satisfies
   325	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-physical-bound}
   326	    0\le J(g)\le R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T(g)^{\alpha/2}<\infty.
   327	  \end{equation}
   328	  The energy over exactly this full class satisfies
   329	  \begin{equation}\label{E:occupation-own-energy}
   330	    0<\mathcal{E}_\star^{\mathcal{O}}
   331	    :=\sup_{g\in\mathcal{O}}\big(J(g)-T(g)/2\big)
   332	    \le R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}<\infty.
   333	  \end{equation}
   334	\end{proposition}
   335	
   336	\begin{proof}
   337	  The map $s\mapsto b(g_s)$ is measurable by continuity of the squared gradient
   338	  norm. Also $\int_0^1\|g_s\|_{H^1}^2\ud s = 1+T(g)$. Use a separably valued
   339	  strong representative and replace exceptional null times by one fixed real
   340	  unit compact bump. Joint measurable spatial representatives exist: approximate
   341	  this Bochner $L^2$ field by simple $H^1$-valued functions with summable
   342	  $L^2(0,1;H^1)$ errors, and choose measurable spatial versions for their
   343	  countably many values. A subsequence has a measurable spacetime $L^2$ limit,
   344	  and for a.e. $s$ its spatial $L^2$ class is $g_s$.
   345	  Lemma~\ref{L:spatial-physical-pair} makes every pairing independent of the
   346	  spatial versions. The continuous pairing map on the separable space $H^1\times
   347	  H^1$ from Proposition~\ref{P:spatial-four-linear} consequently gives a
   348	  measurable function of $(s,t)$ agreeing a.e. with the nonnegative physical
   349	  integral.
   350	
   351	  Set $F(s) = b(g_s)^{\alpha/4}$. Equations~\eqref{E:spatial-homogeneous-bound}
   352	  and~\eqref{E:spatial-square-CS} give $B_\Gamma(g_s^2,g_t^2) \le
   353	  R_{\mathrm{sp}}F(s)F(t)$. Since $0 < \alpha/2 < 1$, concavity on the unit time
   354	  interval yields $\int_0^1F^2 = \int_0^1b(g_s)^{\alpha/2}\ud s \le
   355	  T(g)^{\alpha/2}$. Now use $2F(s)F(t) \le F(s)^2+F(t)^2$ and the exact row
   356	  bound \eqref{E:occupation-kernel-row}, whose column bound is the same because
   357	  $K_\star$ is even, to obtain \eqref{E:occupation-physical-bound}. Positive
   358	  Tonelli is valid before finiteness is known. Null-time modifications affect
   359	  only a product-null set, so they cannot change $J$.
   360	
   361	  The scalar maximum of $R_\star R_{\mathrm{sp}}T^{\alpha/2}-T/2$ over $T \ge 0$
   362	  is $R_\star^{2/(2-\alpha)}\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{sp}}$, by the same
   363	  differentiation as~\eqref{E:spatial-energy-map}. This bounds the occupation
   364	  supremum from above. For positivity take a constant-in-time unit compact
   365	  profile and its spatial dilation $U_\ell$. Its $J$ is $J_0\ell^\alpha
   366	  A_{\mathrm{sp}}(g)$, where $J_0 = \int_0^1\int_0^1K_\star(s-t)\ud s\ud t \in
   367	  (0,\infty)$, while $T = \ell^2b(g)$. For sufficiently small $\ell > 0$,
   368	  $\alpha < 2$ makes $J-T/2 > 0$. Thus, the nonempty supremum is a positive
   369	  finite real number. This is a comparison bound; no attaining profile or
   370	  equality in it has been asserted. No spatial point trace or rough stochastic
   371	  evolution was used. This proves Proposition~\ref{P:occupation-physical-class}.
   372	\end{proof}

   374	For zero covariance all spatial pairings vanish and set $R_{\mathrm{sp}} = 0$.
   375	The spatial and occupation energies are zero suprema of $-b/2$ and $-T/2$: small
   376	spatial dilations of one fixed unit compact profile make these energies tend to
   377	zero, with the profile constant in time for the latter. No zero-gradient unit
   378	state is used. The temporal identities remain valid, and the moment model is the
   379	free case already treated.

    29	  equals `R_⋆`, attained at `s = 1/2`), with `K_⋆` integrable on `[0,1/2]`

    86	/-- The integrand of `E:occupation-damped-kernel`:
    87	`e^{-(λ + λ²/(2D))|u|} λ^{a-1}` (lines 284-287). -/
    88	def kstarIntegrand (a D u l : ℝ) : ℝ :=
    89	  Real.exp (-(l + l ^ 2 / (2 * D)) * |u|) * l ^ (a - 1)

    95	  if u = 0 then 0 else (Real.Gamma a)⁻¹ * ∫ l in Ioi (0 : ℝ), kstarIntegrand a D u l

    97	/-- The row integral `∫_0^1 K_⋆(s-t) dt` of `E:occupation-kernel-row`. -/

   438	      pairing Γ f h = pairing Γ f' h') ∧

   116	theorem cross_eq_convolution (F G : Rd d → ℝ) :
   117	    (fun y => ∫ x, F x * G (x - y)) =
   118	      convolution F (fun x => G (-x)) (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) volume := by

   124	theorem cross_integrable (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] {F G : Rd d → ℝ}
   125	    (hF : Continuous F) (hFs : HasCompactSupport F) (hG : Continuous G)
   126	    (hGs : HasCompactSupport G) : Integrable (fun y => ∫ x, F x * G (x - y)) Γ := by
   127	  rw [cross_eq_convolution]
   128	  refine Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport ?_ ?_

   130	      (ContinuousLinearMap.lsmul ℝ ℝ) hF.locallyIntegrable (hG.comp continuous_neg)

   137	  (hF.mul (hG.comp (continuous_id.sub continuous_const))).integrable_of_hasCompactSupport
   138	    hFs.mul_right

   143	theorem spatialPair_quad (Γ : Measure (Rd d)) [IsLocallyFiniteMeasure Γ] {Q P : Rd d → ℝ}

   148	        t ^ 2 * spatialPair Γ P P := by
   149	  have hin : ∀ y, ∫ x, (Q x + t * P x) * (Q (x - y) + t * P (x - y)) =
   150	      (∫ x, Q x * Q (x - y)) + (t * ((∫ x, Q x * P (x - y)) + ∫ x, P x * Q (x - y)) +
   151	        t ^ 2 * ∫ x, P x * P (x - y)) := by

   153	    have i1 := inner_integrable hQ hQs hQ y
   154	    have i2 := inner_integrable hQ hQs hP y
   155	    have i3 := inner_integrable hP hPs hQ y
   156	    have i4 := inner_integrable hP hPs hP y
   157	    have e : (fun x => (Q x + t * P x) * (Q (x - y) + t * P (x - y))) = fun x =>
